content.title: About
content.content: Canned chicken noodle soup is a ready‑to‑eat soup packed in a sealed can. It contains chicken broth, small noodles, pieces of chicken meat, and vegetables. Made according to a traditional recipe, it retains aroma and nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows the soup to be stored for 2‑3 years without refrigeration.
The broth is often enhanced with monosodium glutamate for flavor.
Noodles are usually small so they soften quickly in hot water.
Canned soups are popular for camping, office lunches, and emergency kits.
Some manufacturers add a small amount of vitamin C to preserve color.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Chicken pieces provide easily digestible animal protein important for tissue repair.

items.title: Electrolytes
items.content: The broth supplies sodium and potassium, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken broth is rich in B6 and B12 vitamins, supporting normal metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from the noodles give a fast source of energy, useful during physical activity.

items.title: Soothing effect
items.content: A warm broth can be comforting and may help ease mild cold symptoms.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned soups often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: To ensure long shelf life, preservatives may be added, which some people prefer to avoid.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to poultry should avoid this product.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Sensitive individuals may experience headaches or flushing from MSG.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Open the can, pour the contents into a pot and bring to a boil for 3‑5 minutes. Optionally garnish with fresh herbs, green onions, or a dash of hot sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 2‑3 days.
